title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a handwritten sheet of 'Questions', marked 'À revoir' in the margin. It is written on the back of a Bourbaki typescript (Tribu 59, Systèmes de racines). The topic is the motivic Galois theory programme: which 'points' (⊗-points, i.e. fibre functors) the Tannakian category of motives has, according to the coefficient field, and what extra structure each kind of realization carries. In modern terms, 'pts^⊗ à valeurs dans K' means fibre functors ω: Mot → (K-modules), i.e. K-points of the motivic Galois gerbe. The page lists them as follows.
(1) Characteristic p > 0. ⊗-points with values in a field k of characteristic p should correspond to motivic points with values in W(k) carrying a semi-linear structure (F, V). This is crystalline / Dieudonné-module cohomology, with Frobenius F and Verschiebung V; the bracket 'foncteurs des groupes formels' refers to Dieudonné theory of formal groups as the H^1 model. A variant is a parenthetical I read as 'en corps des fonctions' (?). From these one passes (squiggly arrow) to 'generalized motivic points' with values in k itself, carrying a filtered structure, i.e. mod-p de Rham / Hodge-type filtrations induced by (F, V). The phrase 'en un sens cat. ...' (perhaps 'division' or 'dérivée') is illegible.
(2) Characteristic 0. ⊗-points with values in k correspond to motivic points in k with a filtered structure: the de Rham realization with its Hodge filtration, i.e. a fibre functor to filtered vector spaces.
(3) Archimedean place. ⊗-points with values in C equipped with complex conjugation (= the Galois group at ∞) are equivalent to three things: motivic points with values in R; or with values in C together with F_∞ (the real Frobenius / infinite Frobenius on Betti cohomology); or with values in Z (the integral Betti lattice).
(4) 'Points banaux' (ordinary points) are points with values in Z_ℓ, with ℓ prime to the residue characteristics, or in Q_ℓ: the ℓ-adic étale realizations.
(5) Important special case: points with values in finite fields F_q correspond to points with values in W(F_q) with semi-linear structure (F, V), i.e. crystalline cohomology over F_q.
Purpose: to organize all the classical cohomology theories as fibre functors, possibly with extra structure, on a single Tannakian category of motives. This is the 'system of realizations' philosophy.
errors: The page consists of questions and heuristics, not claims with proofs. The equivalence 'C with complex conjugation ⟺ R-points ⟺ C with F_∞ ⟺ Z-points' is loose. Galois descent gives the R-structure. The Z-valued Betti lattice is extra integral information and is not equivalent to the others, and Z-valued fibre functors do not fit the field-valued Tannakian formalism.

The correspondence between ⊗-points in characteristic p and W(k)-points with (F, V) presupposes integral, crystalline realizations. These behave well only under smoothness/properness and torsion-freeness hypotheses, which are not developed here.

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a 'generalized motivic point' in characteristic p: a filtered k-valued fibre functor obtained from the (F, V)-W(k)-valued one, with a categorical sense he leaves unspecified. This anticipates Mazur-type links between Frobenius and Hodge filtration and filtered fibre functors in characteristic p. As far as can be read, it is not developed further.
missed.quote: pts motiviques généralisés (en un sens cat. ...) dans k, avec structure filtrée
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly of historical interest. It shows that by around 1965–70 Grothendieck viewed crystalline (F, V)-structures and Hodge filtrations as 'points' of the motivic gerbe. That is relevant to the history of p-adic Hodge theory and to filtered/F-zip fibre functors (e.g. G-zips of Pink–Wedhorn–Ziegler), but the mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clear, early, programmatic list of realizations as fibre functors with extra structure: Betti with F_∞ and Z-lattice, filtered de Rham, crystalline with (F, V), ℓ-adic. It also contains the hint of filtered 'generalized points' in characteristic p. All of this is now standard (Saavedra, Deligne, Jannsen, Fontaine, Mazur–Ogus), and Grothendieck's authorship of the vision is known, so the page offers modest historical interest only.
